title: Surface failed record/delete/bump/save actions instead of console.error only
body:
## Summary
Five mutation handlers in the build dashboard and build pipeline panel swallow failures into console.error; the user sees nothing happen.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/index.tsx:169 (record), :178 (delete), :193 (bump-version) and src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildConfigSelector/index.tsx:123 (save profile), :133 (delete profile) catch the apiFetch error and only log it. A failed Record leaves the form open with no message; a failed bump leaves the version panel unchanged with no reason. The read paths were fixed this round (cb575e83, b5a40d5a) with InlineErrorRetry; the mutation paths are the un-migrated half of the same rule (law failure-not-empty-success). Fixed = each handler sets an action-error state rendered through the shared InlineErrorRetry (retry re-runs the action).

## Flow
- mock the POST/DELETE to return {success:false,error}
- click Record / Delete / Patch / Save Profile
- observe: no role=alert, UI unchanged
- fix: actionError state + InlineErrorRetry per panel

## Expected impact
Operators learn a write failed (locked DB, validation) instead of assuming it landed. Could break: tests asserting no alert on these panels (none found).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every failed mutation is reported to the user
Before: 5/5 mutation handlers report nothing (grep console.error in the two index.tsx files)
After: expected 0/5 silent, measured by a failing-fetch test per action
Method: simulation - walked the 5 catch blocks; the build would need 5 new harness cases, beyond this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: failing-fetch mock per action asserting a role=alert naming the error (same harness as build-history-fetch-failure.test.tsx)

title: Confirm before deleting a build row or a build profile
body:
## Summary
Deleting a recorded build or a whole build profile is one click with no confirmation and no undo.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/BuildRow.tsx:123 calls onDelete(build.id) directly, which issues DELETE /api/packaging/history?id= (src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/index.tsx:170). src/components/modules/game-systems/PlatformProfileCard.tsx:221 calls onDelete(profile.id) -> DELETE /api/packaging/profiles (src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildConfigSelector/index.tsx:124). Build rows are the size-trend and version authority (fd810996): deleting one silently changes the version and the regression baseline. The shared ui/ConfirmDialog exists for exactly this. Fixed = both Delete buttons open ConfirmDialog naming the build/profile.

## Flow
- expand a build row
- click Delete
- row is gone, DELETE already sent
- fix: ConfirmDialog first; DELETE only on confirm

## Expected impact
Prevents accidental loss of history that drives version and size-regression verdicts. Could break: e2e that clicks Delete directly (grep e2e for exe-path/delete).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no accidental irreversible delete
Before: 2/2 delete buttons send DELETE on the first click
After: expected 0/2 send before confirm
Method: simulation - read both click paths; a component test is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: click Delete and assert fetch DELETE count 0 until ConfirmDialog confirm, then 1

title: Platform card shows 0% red for a platform whose only cooks were cancelled
body:
## Summary
PlatformBreakdown renders successRate 0 as a red 0% bar for a platform with only cancelled builds, where nothing was decided.

## Description
getBuildStats rates per platform as success/(success+failed) and returns 0 when that is 0 (src/lib/packaging/build-history-store.ts:471). PlatformStats has no decided/cancelled field (src/lib/packaging/build-history-store.ts:114-123), so src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/PlatformBreakdown.tsx:13-27 cannot tell "0 of 4 succeeded" from "nothing decided" and paints successRateColor(0). The top-level Metrics row was fixed for the same case this round (75dda790). Fixed = PlatformStats carries decided/cancelled; the card shows '-' plus "N cancelled".

## Flow
- seed one platform with 2 cancelled cooks only
- open Build History
- card reads 0% in error colour
- fix: add decided to PlatformStats (store) and branch in PlatformBreakdown

## Expected impact
Removes a false failure signal on platforms with aborted cooks. Touches src/lib/packaging/build-history-store.ts (outside this context's paths), hence lane B.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - per-platform rate matches what was decided
Before: all-cancelled platform -> 0% red (walked from store :471)
After: expected '-' with cancelled count
Method: simulation - store and card read; the seed test lives in build-row-truth.test.tsx style
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: seed sqlite with cancelled-only platform, render PlatformBreakdown, assert no 0%

title: Record form config options derive from CONFIG_OPTIONS, not a literal list
body:
## Summary
The Record form hard-codes the four build configs that CONFIG_OPTIONS already enumerates.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/RecordBuildForm.tsx:70-73 lists <option>Development/DebugGame/Shipping/Test</option> literally while src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildConfigSelector/constants.ts:16-21 is the typed BuildConfig list the profile editor uses. A config added to BuildConfig appears in profiles but cannot be recorded manually. Fixed = map CONFIG_OPTIONS.

## Flow
- compare the two lists
- fix: CONFIG_OPTIONS.map(o => <option value={o.value}>)

## Expected impact
Manual records stay in step with profile configs. Could break nothing visible today (lists identical).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one enumeration of build configs
Before: 2 lists (1 typed, 1 literal)
After: 1 typed list
Method: probe - read both lists
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: Record form option values equal CONFIG_OPTIONS values

title: Remove the unreachable 'errors' sort key
body:
## Summary
SortKey includes 'errors' and the sorter handles it, but no header ever emits it.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/types.ts:3 declares 'errors'; src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/index.tsx:103 sorts on it; src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/HistoryTab.tsx renders SortableHeader for platform/config/size/duration/date only. errorCount has no production writer (BuildComparison.tsx comment, build-row-truth.test.tsx), so a header would sort on zeros. Fixed = drop the variant and branch.

## Flow
- grep "'errors'" in BuildHistoryDashboard: 2 hits, 0 emitters
- fix: remove from SortKey and the switch

## Expected impact
Less dead surface. Could break nothing (zero consumers).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no unreachable sort branch
Before: 1 SortKey variant with 0 emitters
After: 0
Method: probe - grep "'errors'" across BuildHistoryDashboard/ = types.ts:3, index.tsx:103 only
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: typecheck after removal (exhaustive switch) + grep 0 hits

title: Say why a profile card has no UAT command when generation throws
body:
## Summary
generateUATCommand failures are swallowed, so the profile card silently omits the UAT Command section.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildConfigSelector/index.tsx:46-48 wraps generateUATCommand in try { } catch { /* skip */ }; src/components/modules/game-systems/PlatformProfileCard.tsx:164 renders the preview only when uatCommand is truthy. A profile the generator rejects looks identical to one that has no command concept. Fixed = keep the error message per profile and render it in the card where the command would be.

## Flow
- make generateUATCommand throw for a profile
- expand the card
- no UAT section, no reason
- fix: uatErrors map + a one-line reason in the card

## Expected impact
Operators see the profile is unpackageable before pressing Package. Could break nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - generator failure is visible
Before: 1 silent catch; reason shown 0/1
After: reason shown 1/1
Method: simulation - read the catch and the card guard
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: vi.mock uat-command-generator to throw, assert the card shows the message

title: Expose state on expand toggles, sort headers and icon-only refresh buttons
body:
## Summary
Ten controls in this context carry no accessible state or name: 2 expand toggles, 6 sort headers, 2 icon-only refresh buttons.

## Description
src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/BuildRow.tsx:21 and src/components/modules/game-systems/PlatformProfileCard.tsx:102 toggle expansion without aria-expanded (the card's chevron button has no name at all). src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/SortableHeader.tsx:13 conveys the active sort by colour/chevron only (no aria-sort on a columnheader). src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/index.tsx:222 and src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildConfigSelector/index.tsx:229 are icon-only RefreshCw buttons with no aria-label. grep aria-expanded|aria-sort|aria-label="Refresh over the context = 0 hits.

## Flow
- screen reader on the History table: headers announce no sort; rows announce no expanded state
- fix: aria-expanded on toggles, aria-label on icon buttons, aria-sort via role=columnheader wrapper

## Expected impact
Keyboard/SR users can operate the dashboard. Could break nothing visual.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - controls expose name and state
Before: 0/10 controls expose state/name (grep 0 hits)
After: 10/10
Method: probe - grep over the context paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: getByRole(button,{expanded}) / getByRole(button,{name:/refresh/i}) for each control

title: Context map names build-history API routes that do not exist
body:
## Summary
context-map.json api_surface lists /api/packaging/build-history{,/stats,/trend}; the real route is /api/packaging/history with action= params.

## Description
context-map.json (build-history-config.api_surface) claims GET/POST /api/packaging/build-history, GET .../stats, GET .../trend. src/app/api/packaging/ contains cook-jobs, execute, history, preflight, profiles, schedule, smoke-test - no build-history. The dashboard reads /api/packaging/history?action=dashboard (src/components/modules/game-systems/BuildHistoryDashboard/index.tsx:133). Agents scoping by the map look for routes that are not there. The context map is director/scan-owned (edit = architecture escalation).

## Flow
- ls src/app/api/packaging/
- compare to api_surface
- fix: rescan or correct api_surface to /api/packaging/history (GET action=dashboard|list|stats|trend, POST action=record|bump-version|set-budget, DELETE ?id=)

## Expected impact
Correct routing for future agents. Could break nothing in code.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - map matches the tree
Before: 4/4 listed endpoints absent
After: 0/4
Method: probe - ls of the api folder
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
context-map.json build-history-config.api_surface: "GET /api/packaging/build-history, POST /api/packaging/build-history, GET /api/packaging/build-history/stats, GET /api/packaging/build-history/trend"
ls src/app/api/packaging/ -> cook-jobs execute history preflight profiles schedule smoke-test
instrument: rescan context map; assert every api_surface path resolves under src/app/api
